title: The Secret Light of Old Timber
paras: During the French [[revolution|Revolution]], religious buildings were often taken over and their contents removed. Imagine a damp cellar in such a building, with the wooden [[remains|remains]] of shelves slowly decaying. This is a hypothetical scene, not a documented event. Under suitable conditions, such timber could glow faintly. Unlike [[sparkling|sparkling]] crystals reflecting a lantern, it could give off light in complete darkness.

The explanation lies in certain fungi that grow through dead wood. Their fine threads release substances that break down its tough structure, allowing nutrients to be absorbed. A chemical reaction within the fungus also releases energy as greenish light. Outdoors, the same process can turn a rotting [[stump|stump]] into a dim natural lamp, especially on warm, damp nights.

To investigate this phenomenon, a museum might use a research [[grant|grant]] to recreate cellar conditions. Its scientific director and [[deputy|deputy]] could compare timber samples at different temperatures. A camera's automatic [[default|default]] may produce images too dark to reveal the glow, so longer exposures are needed. Drying the wood can reduce fungal activity; restoring moisture may [[reverse|reverse]] that decline if the fungus is still alive.

Yet glowing timber is not an invitation to taste what grows on it. It would be [[rash|rash]] to assume that a natural light signals safety: eating unidentified fungi can cause people to [[vomit|vomit]] or become seriously ill. For historians, the glow offers something safer—a physical explanation for strange lights that earlier visitors might have understood as signs of a haunting.
zh: 法国大革命期间，宗教建筑常被接管，其中的物品也被搬走。请设想这样一座建筑里有一个潮湿的地窖，木架的残余部分正在慢慢腐烂。这是假设的场景，并非有史料记载的事件。在适宜的条件下，这类木材可能发出微光。与反射灯笼光线、闪闪发亮的晶体不同，它即使在完全黑暗的环境中也可能发光。
原因在于某些生长在枯死木材中的真菌。它们细密的菌丝释放出一些物质，分解木材坚韧的结构，从而吸收养分。真菌体内的一种化学反应还会以淡绿色光的形式释放能量。在户外，同样的过程能把腐烂的树桩变成一盏昏暗的天然灯，尤其是在温暖潮湿的夜晚。
为了研究这一现象，博物馆可以利用研究拨款重现地窖环境。科学研究主管及其副手可以比较不同温度下的木材样本。相机自动采用的默认设置可能会使照片太暗，无法显示微光，因此需要延长曝光时间。使木材干燥可以降低真菌的活性；如果真菌仍然存活，恢复湿度可能让其活性重新提高。
不过，发光的木材并不是在邀请人们品尝上面生长的东西。贸然认为天然的光意味着安全，是轻率的：食用未经辨认的真菌可能导致呕吐或严重疾病。对于历史研究者而言，这种微光提供了更安全的收获——它从物理层面解释了那些奇异的光，而过去的访客可能曾把它们理解为闹鬼的迹象。

q.s: Decaying wood can give off light without an external light source.
q.why: 首段指出木材在完全黑暗中也能发光。

q.s: The fungi obtain nutrients without changing the structure of the wood.
q.why: 第二段说明真菌分解木材结构以吸收养分。

q.s: Most visitors to abandoned religious buildings believed the green light brought good luck.
q.why: 文章未提多数访客是否认为绿光带来好运。
